cards.text: Twenty years. That's how long Solomon, king of Israel and son of David, has been building the house of the LORD and his own palace. Both are done, and friend, this man is NOT putting the hammer down.

cards.question: Hiram, king of Tyre, had given Solomon some cities. What does Solomon do with them?

answers.text: Rebuilds them and settles Israelites there
Hands them back to Hiram as a gift
Leaves them empty and falling apart

cards.text: Next, Solomon heads out to a place called Hamath-zobah.

cards.question: When Solomon goes to Hamath-zobah, he captures it.

cards.text: Then the building list just keeps going: Tadmor in the wilderness, store cities, cities for his chariots and horses, and Upper and Lower Beth-horon fortified with walls, gates and bars. Whatever he desired to build in Jerusalem, Lebanon and all through his land, it's on the list. Me? I fold ONE cookie box and I need to sit down.
Now, about the people still left in the land from the Hittites, Amorites, Perizzites, Hivites and Jebusites. They're not Israelites.

cards.question: What does Solomon do with the descendants of those nations still in the land?

answers.text: Sends them out of the land

cards.question: Solomon puts the Israelites to slave labor too.
Solomon keeps the Israelites out of slave labor. They're his men of ___, the leaders of his captains and the commanders of his chariots and cavalry.

cards.text: Israelites are his chief officers too: 250 supervisors. TWO HUNDRED FIFTY! My whole bakery has one supervisor, and it's the oven timer, and it yells at me every eleven minutes.
Then Solomon brings his wife, the daughter of Pharaoh, king of Egypt, up from the City of David. He moves her into a palace he built just for her.

cards.question: Solomon says his wife, Pharaoh's daughter, must not live in the house of David. Why not?

answers.text: The places the ark has entered are holy
The house of David is too small for her
She asked him for a palace of her own

cards.text: At that time, Solomon offers burnt offerings to the LORD on the altar he built in front of the portico. Twenty years of building, and now the altar's doing what it was built for.

cards.question: Solomon keeps the daily requirement for offerings according to the commandment of ___.
Besides Sabbaths and New Moons, Solomon keeps the three annual appointed feasts. Which of these is one of them?

cards.text: Next, Solomon sets up the temple crew: priests in divisions over their service, Levites to offer praise and minister before the priests, and gatekeepers by divisions at each gate. That's not just a temple anymore, friend. That's a WORK SCHEDULE.

cards.question: Solomon sets up the priests, Levites and gatekeepers this way because it was the command of ___, the man of God.
How closely do the priests and Levites follow King Solomon's command, even about the treasuries?

answers.text: They don't turn aside from it at all
They follow it except for the treasuries
They follow it only on the feast days

cards.question: From the day the foundation was laid, all of Solomon's work is carried out until the house of the LORD is completed.

cards.text: Then Solomon goes to Ezion-geber and Eloth, on the coast of Edom. Twenty years of building, and NOW the man goes to the coast.

cards.question: Out on the coast of Edom, who sends Solomon ships and crews of experienced sailors?
Hiram's sailors go with Solomon's servants to ___ and get gold there.

cards.text: They deliver 450 talents of gold to King Solomon. FOUR HUNDRED FIFTY! The fanciest thing in my old junk drawer was a coupon that expired years ago.

findings.problem: The right answer, "The places the ark has entered are holy," is the only answer with Bible-sounding words (ark, holy). The two wrong answers are everyday household reasons, so the right answer stands out without reasoning.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike. None should sound more like the Bible, or more modern, than the others.

findings.problem: "Twenty years of building, and now the altar's doing what it was built for" implies the altar is only now being used for offerings after twenty years. 8:12 says only that Solomon offered burnt offerings "at that time." Offerings were already made on it at the dedication (2 Chronicles 7:1, 7), so the line says something the text shows is wrong.

rule.text: Papa Dorin can retell in his own words and fill in what the text clearly implies. Scene-setting details are fine. He never says anything the text shows is wrong.

findings.problem: The question says the priests and Levites themselves follow the command. 8:15 says only "They did not turn aside from the king's command regarding the priests or the Levites." Who "they" are is left open, and the command is about the priests and Levites.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: The question's words "even about the treasuries" rule out the wrong answer "They follow it except for the treasuries." They also point to the right answer.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: This summary story card for the building list (8:4-6) is 4 sentences, including the joke. The bite-sized rule says other story cards are 1 to 2 sentences. But the docs' own good summary example (Genesis 5) is also 4 sentences, and a summary card is called one beat.
findings.question: Does the 1 to 2 sentence limit apply to summary story cards for long stretches, or can they run longer, as the Genesis 5 example does?
